lessons.title: Promoting Listings on Social Media
lessons.body: Social media is your free billboard. In Africa, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp are where buyers spend time. Start by creating a business page on Facebook and Instagram. Use your phone to take clear photos of your products on a plain background (a white wall works). Post at least 3 times a week. Mix product photos, short videos (15-30 seconds) showing the item in use, and customer testimonials. Use hashtags like #ShopNigeria, #JumiaFinds, or #NairobiFashion to reach local buyers. Join Facebook groups for buying and selling in your city. For example, 'Lagos Buy and Sell' or 'Accra Online Market'. Post your items there with a price and 'DM to order'. Respond to comments and messages within 1 hour. Use WhatsApp Business to set up a catalog and auto-replies. Share your listings in WhatsApp status and groups. Offer a small discount for customers who share your post. Track which posts get the most engagement using Facebook Insights. Double down on what works. Remember, consistency beats perfection. Even a simple post with a clear price and a call to action can bring sales.

lessons.title: Using eBay and Amazon Ads
lessons.body: If you sell on eBay or Amazon, paid ads can boost your visibility. Start with eBay Promoted Listings. You set an ad rate (percentage of sale price) â typically 2-5% for most categories. eBay only charges when your item sells, so it's low risk. For Amazon, use Sponsored Products. You bid on keywords buyers search for. Start with a daily budget of $5 (about 4,000 Naira or 60 Rand). Use automatic targeting first to let Amazon find keywords, then switch to manual after 2 weeks. Keep your ad rate competitive: if you're not getting impressions, increase your bid by 10% every few days. Monitor your ACoS (Advertising Cost of Sale). Aim for ACoS below 30% â meaning you spend 30 cents for every dollar of sales. If ACoS is higher, lower your bid or improve your listing. Use negative keywords to avoid wasted spend. For example, if you sell phone cases, add 'free' as a negative keyword. Always ensure your product images are high quality and your title includes key search terms. Ads work best when your organic listing is already optimized. Test with a small budget, then scale what works.

lessons.title: Email Marketing for Resellers
lessons.body: Email marketing is not dead â it's a direct line to repeat buyers. Start by collecting emails. Offer a 10% discount code for signing up. Use a free tool like Mailchimp (up to 500 subscribers) or Brevo (formerly Sendinblue). Add a sign-up form to your social media bio and your online store. When a customer buys, ask for their email. Send a welcome email immediately with your best-selling items and the discount code. Then, send a newsletter every 2 weeks. Include new arrivals, special offers, and useful tips (e.g., 'How to care for your leather bag'). Personalize with the customer's name. Segment your list: buyers vs. window shoppers. Send buyers a 'thank you' email 3 days after delivery and ask for a review. For window shoppers, send a cart abandonment email after 24 hours. In Africa, mobile is key â make sure your emails are mobile-friendly. Use clear, large buttons. Test subject lines: 'Your 10% off expires tonight' works better than 'Newsletter'. Track open rates and click-through rates. Aim for 20% open rate. Clean your list every 3 months by removing people who haven't opened in 6 months. Consistency builds trust and sales.

lessons.title: Cross-Promoting Across Platforms
lessons.body: Don't put all your eggs in one basket. Cross-promotion means using one platform to drive traffic to another. For example, post a TikTok video of you packing an order, then say 'Link in bio to shop'. On Instagram, share a photo of a product and tell followers to 'Swipe up' to your WhatsApp catalog. On Facebook, create a post that links to your eBay listing. Use the same handle across all platforms for easy recognition. When you make a sale on Jumia, include a thank-you card with your Instagram handle and a 5% discount code for their next purchase on your own website. Run a contest: 'Follow us on Instagram and tag a friend to win a free phone case'. Use WhatsApp status to announce a flash sale on your Facebook page. Create a Linktree (free) to house all your links in one place. Share your YouTube videos on LinkedIn if you sell B2B. Cross-promotion works because different platforms attract different audiences. A buyer on Facebook might not know you're on TikTok. By cross-promoting, you increase touchpoints and build brand recall. Track which platform sends the most traffic using UTM links (use Google's Campaign URL Builder). Double down on the best performers.

lessons.title: Running Sales and Discounts
lessons.body: Discounts can boost sales, but use them wisely. A common mistake is to discount too often, which trains customers to wait for sales. Instead, plan your promotions around events: Black Friday, Christmas, Ramadan, or back-to-school. Announce your sale 3 days in advance on social media and email. Use a countdown timer on your posts. For example, '24 hours only: 20% off all shoes'. Set a clear start and end time. Use a discount code like 'AFRICA20' to track sales. On eBay, you can run a 'Markdown Sale' event â eBay will promote it. On Amazon, use 'Coupons' or 'Lightning Deals'. For your own website, use WooCommerce or Shopify's discount features. Don't discount your best-sellers too much â you'll lose profit. Instead, bundle slow-moving items with popular ones: 'Buy a phone case, get a screen protector 50% off'. Offer free shipping instead of a discount â it often feels more valuable. After the sale, send a 'thank you' email to buyers and a 'sorry you missed it' email to non-buyers with a smaller offer. Track your profit margin before and after. A sale that increases revenue but kills profit is not a win. Test small discounts (10%) first, then increase if needed.

lessons.title: Leveraging Influencers and Affiliates
lessons.body: Influencers can put your products in front of thousands of potential buyers. Start with micro-influencers (1,000 to 10,000 followers) â they are cheaper and often have higher engagement. In Africa, many micro-influencers charge $20 to $50 (about 15,000 to 40,000 Naira) per post. Look for influencers in your niche: fashion, tech, home goods. Send them a free product in exchange for an honest review. Use a simple contract: they post 1 photo and 1 story, tag you, and share a discount code. Track sales using their unique code. For affiliates, use a platform like ShareASale or Refersion. You can also run a simple affiliate program manually: give your best customers a 10% commission for every sale they refer. Use a Google Form to sign them up. Provide them with ready-made posts and images. Pay them via mobile money (M-Pesa, MTN MoMo) or PayPal. Set a cookie duration of 30 days so you get credit for delayed purchases. Always disclose paid partnerships â it's required by law in many countries and builds trust. Start with 3-5 influencers, measure results, and scale the ones that bring sales. Don't just look at likes â look at clicks and conversions.

quiz.q: Which social media platform is most widely used for buying and selling in many African countries?
quiz.explanation: Facebook and its groups are extremely popular for local buying and selling across Africa.

quiz.q: What is a good first step to promote your listings on social media?
options: A) Create a business page on Facebook and Instagram
quiz.explanation: Creating a business page is free and gives you a professional presence to post listings.

quiz.q: How often should you post on social media to see results?
options: B) At least 3 times a week
D) Only when you have a sale
quiz.explanation: Consistency is key; posting at least 3 times a week keeps your audience engaged.

quiz.q: What is a good way to track which social media posts work best?
quiz.explanation: Facebook Insights provides data on reach, engagement, and clicks to guide your strategy.

quiz.q: On eBay, how does Promoted Listings charge you?
options: B) Only when your item sells
quiz.explanation: eBay Promoted Listings use an ad rate that you pay only after a sale is made.

quiz.q: What is a typical starting daily budget for Amazon Sponsored Products?
quiz.explanation: A $5 daily budget is a low-risk way to test Amazon ads.

quiz.q: What does ACoS stand for in Amazon advertising?
quiz.explanation: ACoS measures ad spend as a percentage of sales; aim for below 30%.

quiz.q: Why should you use negative keywords in Amazon ads?
options: B) To avoid wasted spend on irrelevant searches
quiz.explanation: Negative keywords prevent your ad from showing for searches that are unlikely to convert.

quiz.q: Which free email marketing tool is recommended for up to 500 subscribers?
quiz.explanation: Mailchimp offers a free plan for up to 500 subscribers.

quiz.q: What is a good way to get people to sign up for your email list?
options: B) Send them daily emails without permission
D) Post on social media only
quiz.explanation: Incentives like a discount code encourage sign-ups.

quiz.q: How often should you send a newsletter to your email list?
quiz.explanation: A bi-weekly newsletter keeps you top of mind without overwhelming subscribers.

quiz.q: What is a good subject line for an email?
quiz.explanation: Urgency and personal benefit increase open rates.

quiz.q: What is cross-promotion?
options: A) Using one platform to drive traffic to another
B) Posting the same content everywhere
C) Only selling on one platform
quiz.explanation: Cross-promotion leverages multiple platforms to increase reach and sales.

quiz.q: Which tool can help you house all your links in one place?
quiz.explanation: Linktree is a free tool to create a single landing page for multiple links.

quiz.q: Why is cross-promotion effective?
options: B) Different platforms attract different audiences
quiz.explanation: Each platform has a unique user base, so cross-promotion expands your reach.

quiz.q: What should you include in a thank-you card when shipping an order?
options: A) Your social media handle and a discount code
quiz.explanation: This encourages repeat business and grows your social following.

quiz.q: When is a good time to run a sale?
options: B) Around events like Black Friday or Ramadan
C) Only when you have no stock
quiz.explanation: Aligning sales with major shopping events increases visibility and urgency.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake with discounts?
quiz.explanation: Frequent discounts train customers to wait for sales, reducing full-price purchases.

quiz.q: What is a better alternative to a discount?
quiz.explanation: Free shipping feels valuable and can increase conversions without cutting into product price.

quiz.q: How can you track sales from a specific discount code?
options: A) Use a unique code like 'AFRICA20'
quiz.explanation: Unique codes let you attribute sales to specific promotions.

quiz.q: What is a micro-influencer?
options: B) A celebrity with millions of followers
quiz.explanation: Micro-influencers have smaller but often more engaged audiences and are cheaper to work with.

quiz.q: What is a common payment method for influencers in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Mobile money is widely used and convenient for paying influencers.

quiz.q: What should you provide to affiliates to make their job easier?
quiz.explanation: Providing promotional materials increases the likelihood they will promote effectively.

quiz.q: What is a typical commission for an affiliate?
quiz.explanation: 10% is a common and attractive commission rate for resellers.

quiz.q: Why should you disclose paid partnerships?
options: A) It's required by law and builds trust
quiz.explanation: Disclosure is legally required in many countries and maintains transparency with your audience.

quiz.q: What is a good way to measure influencer success?
options: A) Look at clicks and conversions
quiz.explanation: Clicks and conversions directly show if the influencer drove sales.

quiz.q: What is a good first step before running a sale?
options: A) Announce it 3 days in advance
D) Only post on the day
quiz.explanation: Advance notice builds anticipation and allows customers to plan purchases.

quiz.q: What should you do after a sale ends?
options: A) Send a thank-you email to buyers and a 'sorry you missed it' email to non-buyers
quiz.explanation: Follow-up emails nurture relationships and can recover lost sales.

quiz.q: What is a key metric to track after a sale?
quiz.explanation: Profit margin ensures the sale was financially worthwhile.

quiz.q: What is a good way to test a discount?
options: A) Start with 10% and increase if needed
quiz.explanation: Starting small allows you to gauge response without sacrificing too much profit.
